item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. item.title: Broncos’ Jonathan Cooper Revisits Year-Old Chiefs Controversy With Surprising Public Message
item.description: The Denver Broncos took first place in the AFC West on Sunday with a 28-24 comeback win over the Kansas City Chiefs. Linebacker Jonathon Cooper helped apply late pressure on the final snap, and he was not done speaking afterward. On Monday, he returned to social media with a message aimed at the Chiefs, one that looks back at a moment from last season. Jonathon Cooper apologizes to Chiefs for last year’s posts Cooper took to X on Monday and spoke directly to Kansas City. He also said sorry for what he wrote a season ago. Cooper wrote publicly : “Man all do respect to the Chiefs they are a great team. With hall of famers. Players I’ve aspired to be like. I apologize for my tweets from last year if anyone cares in football matters.” The apology goes back to late December 2025. Denver beat Kansas City 20-13 on Christmas Day, and two days later the Broncos clinched their first AFC West title since 2015 when the Chargers lost to the Texans. https://t.co/RZScFpuLbQ — Jonathon Cooper (@JonathonCooper7) November 2, 2026 Cooper then posted harsh, explicit messages aimed at the Chiefs, who had led the division since 2016. He was enjoying a strong year, with eight sacks and 49 tackles through 16 games. Nov 30, 2025; Landover, Maryland, USA; Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper (0) runs off the field after the game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Sunday’s win gave him a fresh chance to revisit it. A false start on Kansas City tackle Jaylon Moore wiped out a go-ahead touchdown, and Malcolm Roach sacked Patrick Mahomes on the next play to end the game. The Chiefs are also bracing for NFL punishment after several incidents in that game. Still, his road back to the field this fall was far from simple. Cooper returns to Broncos after exempt list stint Cooper was arrested twice in June on domestic violence related charges involving his former girlfriend. He now faces five charges, including a felony count of second-degree assault, and has pleaded not guilty. His trial is set for March. The NFL placed him on the commissioner’s exempt list on Aug. 30, and he missed Denver’s first six games. The league removed him from the list on Oct. 16, and he returned in Week 7 at Arizona. Sunday marked his second game back, and he helped Denver close out the win. On the field, Cooper has been one of Denver’s most productive pass rushers, totaling 31.5 sacks over 81 career games before this season. The league says it will keep monitoring the case, so he could still face discipline. Denver (6-2) leads the AFC West by a half game over Kansas City (5-2). The Broncos visit the Panthers (3-4) on Nov. 8, while the Chiefs, who already made a roster move after the loss , host the Jets (2-6) next. item.title: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - Mark Crow
item.description: The Brooklyn Nets have signed, drafted, and traded for players from virtually every state in the US, and much of the wider world beyond the United States. From Alabama to Wyoming, and from Australia to Ukraine, the Nets have a long and distinguished history of turning over every stone to find the talent needed to succeed in the NBA. From their start in the American Basketball Association (ABA) as the New Jersey Americans and New York Nets to their jump to the NBA as the New Jersey Nets right through to today, the organization has cast their net for talent wide since the inception of the ball club. For this installment of our series documenting the provenience of every Nets player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for Brooklyn. Our focus in this article is Mark Crow. An alum of Duke, he was picked up with the 111th overall selection of the 1977 NBA Draft by the (then) New Jersey (now, Brooklyn) Nets. The California native played the sole season of his pro career with New Jersey, leaving the league as a player afterward. During his time suiting up for the Nets, Crow put up 5.6 points and 1.8 rebounds per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. item.title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 40 - Richard Anderson (1987)
item.description: The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history. To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day. With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover. And for today's article, we will continue with the fourth of eight who wore the No. 40, Richard Anderson. After ending his college career at UC Santa Barbara, he was picked up with the 32nd overall selection of the 1982 NBA Draft by the (then) San Diego (now, Los Angeles) Clippers. The San Pedro, California native played the first season of his pro career with the Clippers. He also played for the Denver Nuggets and abroad before he signed with the Houston Rockets in 1987. His stay with the team lasted until he was cut later that year. During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Anderson wore only jersey No. 40 and put up 2.8 points and 1.5 rebounds per game. item.description: HOUSTON, TX - OCTOBER 25: Houston Texans costumed mascot Toro enters the field during the NFL game between the New York Giants and Houston Texans on October 25, 2026 at Reliant Stadium in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Leslie Plaza Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Houston’s Bye Week : Where does Houston stand vis-a-vis the league after the bye? While Houston took the week off, the chaos didn’t stop. That will likely continue when Houston gets back to their schedule. When they kick-off next Sunday in LA, they will be no better than 2.5 games back of the Jaguars, possibly down 3.5 games. They still have three division games (all at home) left. As for a Wild Card, sitting 11th in the conference does not help their situation. They sit 2.5 games back of New England for the final spot, with Cleveland, Las Vegas and Baltimore still ahead of them. They have three remaining non-conference games, but all of those are on the road and in December/January. While they are a maddening 0-4 at home, they somehow have a winning road record at 2-1. Given that the remainder of the schedule is 6 road games/4 home games, that may not be the worst thing in the world. On the opposite end of the spectrum, Houston holds the 8th pick in the 2027 draft. Just based on numbers, Houston could remain in the draft top 10 if their struggles continue. If the franchise gets solid play from Stroud in spite of bad team play and decides to give him that second contract, it could make Houston game for some wheeling and dealing related to that draft pick. item.title: Three Observations from the way Bayern Munich dismantled Atlético Madrid
item.description: (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) | Getty Images The coordinated denial of space When Diego Simeone chose the lineup and tactics for Atlético Madrid this game, he knew he had to keep Bayern Munich from scoring. Goals goals goals. That’s what it all boils down to. This isn’t Manchester United. When you face the best attack in Europe, and you’re not PSG, you need to think of ways to shut it down. To keep a team like FC Bayern from scoring, there are different things you can do. You can press high and run hard, like Freiburg and Stuttgart did. It always ends poorly. You can pack the box and hope for the best. Sometimes it works, ask Schalke. You can contest the midfield battle and try to win it, which could have worked for Arsenal. Or you go the cynical route, with invisible fouls and fifty-fifty duels, which Borussia Dortmund used to decent effect. None of those represent a silver bullet. No team has beaten the Bavarians yet. So Simeone went for the last possible option, the one easier said than done. He decided to deny key Bayern Munich stars space to operate. Understanding the full tactical scheme would take too many words to describe. What the Spaniards decided was to focus their resources on key threats, mainly the FC Bayern front three. This meant taking attention away from tertiary players like the fullbacks and central defenders, which had its own tactical consequences. Here is how it worked. Alphonso Davies was marked wide with a standoff defender that kept pushing him onto the shoulder. It kept the Canadian from using his pace to get behind the defense, suffocating the left. Meanwhile, Michael Olise, who lacks explosive pace, was tightly marked from the get go, given almost zero room to to actually pass and dribble. Harry Kane was isolated and kept from getting easy shooting angles. This focus came with the tradeoff that players like Konrad Laimer and Dayot Upamecano were given freedom to dominate. Simeone gambled that this was enough. He hoped that the chances which fell to players outside of the Ballon d’Or top 10 would not be converted. Unfortunately he was wrong. The fact is, there were too many chances, and too much space to cover. You cannot deny Bayern Munich everything. And if you commit too hard in one direction, you lose your threat at the other end. Simeone gambled and lost. The margins were against him. Here’s why all of this matters. This performance was the best that one of the finest defensive tacticians in the game could come up with. It still wasn’t enough to keep Bayern Munich from winning comfortably. Despite the injuries, despite a missing coach, despite playing away from home in the UEFA Champions League. item.title: Fenway Sports Group Could Make SHOCKING Move Into Formula 1 as NASCAR Ownership Connection Emerges
item.description: Formula One F1 - United States Grand Prix - Circuit of the Americas, Austin, Texas, U.S. - October 25, 2026 Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas in action during the race IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Jerome Miron Could one of the biggest ownership groups in American sports be preparing to make an even bigger investment in Formula 1? According to a report from The Wall Street Journal , Fenway Sports Group is among several potential buyers currently in discussions with TWG Global about purchasing part of its stake in the Cadillac Formula 1 team. The report was shared by Adam Stern, bringing attention to a potentially significant development that could have major implications for both the future of Cadillac and the growing business side of Formula 1. And for NASCAR fans, there is an especially interesting connection. Fenway Sports Group isn’t just another major sports investment company. The organization owns the Boston Red Sox, Liverpool FC, and a NASCAR team, among several other sporting assets. Now, it could potentially add a stake in one of Formula 1’s newest teams to its portfolio. Fenway Sports Group Could Be Heading Into Formula 1 Fenway Sports Group has built an impressive portfolio across multiple sports, and a potential investment in Cadillac F1 would represent another major step into international motorsports. Cadillac entered Formula 1 in 2026 as the championship’s newest team, becoming the first new full-time constructor to join the grid since Haas in 2016. The team is backed by TWG Global and General Motors, with the Cadillac name bringing another major American manufacturer into the sport. However, the latest report suggests TWG Global could be open to selling part of its ownership stake, with several interested parties reportedly involved in discussions. Fenway Sports Group is among those potential buyers. It remains unclear how much of the team could be made available, what percentage FSG would potentially purchase, or whether an agreement will ultimately be reached. Still, the possibility of another major American sports ownership group getting involved in Formula 1 is certainly worth watching. The NASCAR Connection Makes This Even More Interesting For NASCAR fans, Fenway Sports Group’s potential involvement is particularly interesting because of its existing connection to stock car racing. FSG is associated with Roush Fenway Keselowski Racing, the NASCAR organization that competes in the Cup Series. A potential investment in Cadillac would give the group an even greater presence across two of the biggest motorsports platforms in the world. NASCAR and Formula 1 have both continued to attract significant attention from international audiences, sponsors, and major investors. Having an ownership group connected to both championships could create some fascinating possibilities moving forward. It would also further highlight how major sports organizations are increasingly looking beyond traditional boundaries when it comes to investing in motorsports

item.title: UConn QB Bo Polston retiring from football
item.description: Decatur Central’s Bo Polston poses for a photo Thursday, July 24, 2025, at Decatur Central High School in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co UConn football freshman Bo Polston announced his medical retirement on Instagram this afternoon. The injury is undisclosed. He joined the team in January as an early enrollee. Before Jason Candle became Connecticut head coach, he was committed to Toledo. The three-star gunslinger flipped his commitment to UConn in December 2025 and signed in January. During the Huskies’ 2026 spring game in April, the 6-foot-2, 200-pound shot-caller was sidelined, but returned for fall camp. In his senior year at Decatur Central HS (IN), Polston completed 87 of 132 (65.9%) passes for 1,059 yards, 11 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. The Indiana native also rushed for 411 yards and another six TDs. “After talking with coaches and my family, it is with a heavy heart I have made the decision to medically retire from the game of football,” Polston wrote in his announcement. “[I] want to thank Coach Candle for giving me this opportunity and believing in me as a young man and a football player.”

item.title: Alabama Lands at No. 5 in First CFP Rankings Despite Two Losses
item.description: Photo by: David Leong The Alabama Crimson Tide have officially earned a spot inside the top five of the first College Football Playoff rankings of the 2026 season. Despite already suffering two losses, the selection committee placed Alabama at No. 5, giving Kalen DeBoer’s team an early opportunity to compete for a national championship. At 6-2 overall and 4-2 in SEC play, Alabama has experienced an interesting season. The Crimson Tide started strong but suffered consecutive losses against Georgia and Tennessee, raising questions about their consistency and championship expectations. However, the committee clearly believes Alabama has one of the strongest resumes in the country. Alabama Gets Major Recognition One of the biggest reasons Alabama landed at No. 5 is its impressive collection of victories. The Crimson Tide have defeated Kentucky, Florida State, South Carolina, Mississippi State and Texas A&M. Their 45-17 victory over Kentucky was particularly important. With Kentucky sitting at No. 6 in the first CFP rankings, Alabama holds a valuable head-to-head victory over another highly ranked SEC program. DeBoer has also helped Alabama remain competitive despite the difficult stretch in October. The Crimson Tide responded to their losses against Georgia and Tennessee with a 31-20 victory over Texas A&M. That bounce back performance helped Alabama regain some momentum heading into November. A Huge Opportunity Against LSU Alabama’s next challenge will be another important SEC matchup against LSU on November 7. The Tigers currently sit at No. 14 in the first CFP rankings, making this another opportunity for Alabama to add a quality victory to its playoff resume. item.title: Vikings DC Brian Flores Gets Candid on Facing Bills QB Josh Allen
item.description: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) Getty The Minnesota Vikings will have to put their Week 8 loss behind them as they now have to focus on Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills in Week 9 to avoid losing back-to-back games. Moreover, the Vikings defense will have a major challenge dealing with Allen, who has a passer rating of 101.1 with 1,793 yards, 11 touchdowns and five interceptions in seven games, per StatMuse . Ahead of the Week 9 game against the Bills, Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores spoke about facing Allen and the challenges that the quarterback brings to an opposing defense. “This is the most, or one of the most, dynamic players in our league,” Flores told reporters on Nov. 3 . “He makes a lot of people miss. He breaks a lot of tackles: Big, strong quarterback, huge arm. There’s risk-reward. Pressuring people all the time, every week, and so that’s certainly our play style. I don’t know if we’re going to go too far away from it, but we’re not going to be reckless. “We’re going to understand that with a guy like this, you can have an unblocked defender, and he can make that guy miss. The rest of the coverage, the rest of the rush, we’ve got to do a great job of working through some extended plays because we’re going to have those. You kind of know that going in. But Josh is one of the best players in our league. This is a testament to his work.” Brian Flores on Bills’ Josh Allen’s Growth Over the Years Furthermore, Flores noted the growth that he’s seen from Allen over the years, from the first time he went up against the Bills star while being a coach with the New England Patriots . “I’ve seen him develop,” Flores added. “I was in New England when he started, when he was a rookie and a second-year player. At that time, it was, ‘Hey, keep him in the pocket and make him throw from the pocket because he’s not really that accurate.’ That is certainly not the case anymore. “It’s fun to watch his growth and development, from where he was as a rookie and second-year player to being in the MVP race yearly and having one win, probably likely to win some more. item.title: Mission accomplished: Glastonbury boys soccer wins CCC title after missing 2025 tournament
item.description: Glastonbury boys soccer defeated South Windsor 3-0 for the CCC title at Sage Park in Berlin on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. (Will Aldam/Hearst Connecticut Media) BERLIN - When the season began, Glastonbury boys soccer was looking for redemption. The Guardians finished the 2025 season with a 6-7-4 record, missing the conference tournament after reaching the final in each of the previous two seasons. Expectations were high for Glastonbury from the outset this season, with 13 seniors and 17 returners. On Tuesday, those expectations were met. Glastonbury defeated South Windsor 3-0 at Sage Park to win the CCC championship, its second title in four years. "We talked about it today - championship games don't come around very often and it is an opportunity to honor the history of Glastonbury soccer," Glastonbury coach KC Warren said. "To galvanize this team in its current state and really lay a foundation for the future." The Guardians took a two-goal lead in the first half, with Adam Kukulka and Seweryn Rak scoring. Senior captain Brady Nilsen scored the only goal of the second half, while goalkeeper Jonathan Seymour posted a shutout. "The one thing that we did right, we converted our chances at a higher rate than we did the rest of the season," Warren said. "We may have leveled down a little bit in quality opportunities, but to convert more of them has a big impact. And our goalie stood on his head. He had a great game. It is a great moment for the program." Glastonbury reached the CCC final in three of the last four seasons, winning the title in 2023 and losing to Berlin in 2024. For the large group of seniors, it was a return to the top of the mountain after an unusually mediocre 2025 season. item.title: Gibson Exits After First Period in Matchup in Tampa Bay
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Detroit netminder John Gibson exited the Red Wings game against the Tampa Bay Lightning after the first period with an apparent lower body injury, and has been ruled out for the rest of the game. UPDATE: John Gibson (lower body) will not return to tonight's game. — Detroit Red Wings (@DetroitRedWings) November 4, 2026 The Red Wings started Gibson in the second game of their back-to-back series in Florida, having Daniil Tarasov start in the first game, and step in between the pipes for the second period onward against the Lightning. Gibson blocked 11 of 13 shots faced against the Lightning tonight, with both goals coming from Braden Point, once on the power play, and once at even strength. The Red Wings have given Gibson the nod in net to start ten times this season, excluding tonight, with the netminder accumulating a 4-5-1 record and a 3.37 GAA. Detroit relied heavily on Gibson in the back half of last season after he accumulated a 17-4-1 record from December through January. The veteran would finish the season with a 29-22-4 record on the year, starting the third most games of his career in his age 30 season. While Gibson’s status is not yet known beyond tonight, the Red Wings do have the option to call up exciting goalie prospect Michal Postava if Gibson’s injury lingers beyond the next two nights. Detroit next plays at home against the Las Vegas Golden Knights, and will likely make the call up for Postava, as Tarasov will have played back to back nights in Florida and may not be up to three games in a four day span.
